newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: MORE SHIPS CALLING AT S.AFRICAN NAVAL BASE--MODISE.
newsitem.headline: MORE SHIPS CALLING AT S.AFRICAN NAVAL BASE--MODISE.

text.p: Once shunned by the world's navies, the Simon's Town naval base has become a popular calling place, Defence Minister Joe Modise said on Tuesday.

Answering a question in parliament, Modise said before the first all-race elections in 1994, the international arms embargo had kept navies away from Simon's Town. The only exception was warships from Taiwan, a supporter of the apartheid regime.
Since then, 65 warships from 20 countries as varied as Argentina, Denmark, France, Kenya, Britain and the U.S. had visited the naval base, he said.
But Modise said that after the base's agreement with Britain had expired in the 1970s, only the French had made use of its repair facilities.
"Other countries visit the port on goodwill visits, to conduct combined naval exercises, for minor repairs or rest and recuperation for crews during long deployments.

"It is foreseen that the repair facilities and use of the base for rest and recuperation will increase once multi- and bilateral national and military agreements in support of foreign policy are signed and ratified," Modise said.
